about: Known departures of cPMML (as docs/design/typed-core.md designs it) from JPMML 1.7.7, D1..D22 of §8.5, read by tools/fuzz/compare.py. 'spec': true marks a departure from the PMML 4.4.1 specification itself; every other entry follows the spec where JPMML does not, or is a choice where the spec is silent. A rule matches a non-identical cell: 'kinds' (its class), 'tags_all' / 'tags_any' / 'tags_none' (fnmatch patterns over the case's tags from tools/fuzz/gen.py), 'jpmml' / 'cpmml' / 'column' (regular expressions searched in the cell text or column name), 'cpmml_x' (searched in cPMML's string text of x in the same row: JPMML fails a record as a whole, so a rule about x is checked on x, and covers the other columns of that record), 'unreferenced_field' (a regex whose group 1 is a field name taken from cPMML's cell; the rule matches only if the case never reads that field), 'row' (field -> full-match regex on the input row, N/A for missing) and 'row_any' (full-match regex on any input cell). A rule encodes the value cPMML is DESIGNED to give, so a cell where today's cPMML still has a known bug (B1..B34) does not match and is reported as a finding. v0 rules key on the case's tags, not on the sub-expression that produced the cell; P11's shrinker narrows them. 'measured' records what P0 observed with tools/fuzz/JpmmlOracle.java.

departures.cpmml: numeric mixed-type comparisons in the promoted type, either order
departures.jpmml: converts to the left operand's type: equal(f, double 0.1) is true (double narrowed to float); equal(i, double 3.5) throws TypeCheckException
departures.basis: Functions.html least-restrictive precedence

departures.cpmml: string x number equality compared as text, either order
departures.jpmml: parses the string when the number is the left operand (NumberFormatException on unparsable text)
departures.basis: Functions.html least-restrictive precedence

departures.cpmml: if with a missing condition gives missing (then mapMissingTo/defaultValue)
departures.jpmml: MissingArgumentException: Function "if" cannot accept missing value at position 0 (measured)
departures.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html: "Except as noted below, any missing inputs to a built-in function will result in a missing value being returned."

match.jpmml: MissingArgumentException: Function ""?if""? cannot accept missing value at position 0

departures.cpmml: integers are int64; overflow invalid
departures.jpmml: 32-bit: an integer input 2147483648 or 9007199254740993 fails the record (ValueCheckException under returnInvalid, IllegalArgumentException under asIs; measured); refuses 1e10
departures.basis: XSD integer is unbounded; int64 is the representable subset (Q10)

departures.cpmml: rint, expm1, ln1p, hypot return double
departures.jpmml: rint(3) is 3
departures.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html pseudo-declarations: <DefineFunction name="rint" optype="continuous" dataType="double"> (and the same for expm1, ln1p, hypot)

departures.cpmml: an aggregate's type comes from the declared argument types even when one is skipped (max(int, double missing) is -7.0)
departures.basis: "the least restrictive dataType will be inherited"

departures.cpmml: if has the common type of THEN and ELSE
departures.jpmml: type of the branch taken
departures.basis: static typing; spec silent

departures.cpmml: pow of integers with a negative exponent is invalid and follows invalidValueTreatment
departures.jpmml: InvalidArgumentException: Function "pow" cannot accept "exponent" value of -1 regardless of invalidValueTreatment (measured)
departures.basis: Apply output table (invalidValueTreatment)

departures.cpmml: +-INF against the same INF gives missing; NaN in comparisons gives missing (extrapolation)
departures.jpmml: equal(INF, INF) and equal(NaN, NaN) are both true (measured: Java Double.compare semantics, not IEEE)
departures.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html lessThan: "By definition, INF is taken as greater than any finite number or -INF and -INF is taken as less than any finite number or INF. But any attempt to either with itself is indeterminate and will result in a missing value being returned." For NaN the spec says only "All arithmetic expressions involving NaN will evaluate to NaN" (Transformations.html): the NaN rule is the design's extrapolation

departures.cpmml: an untyped Constant NaN/INF/-INF is a string
departures.jpmml: a number: <Constant>NaN</Constant> in a string DerivedField gives NaN, INF gives Infinity, -INF gives -Infinity (measured)
departures.basis: Transformations.html Constant: "The presence of any non-numeric characters (other than e, E, -, + in scientific notation expressions ) will result in the Constant being treated as a string"; the INF/NaN values are "case insensitive and only meaningful as floating point values ( datatype equal to "float" or "double")"

departures.cpmml: inputs, attributes and Array members use the strict, case-sensitive XSD lexical forms (TRUE, inf, 1d, 1.0 for an integer are invalid); only Constant text accepts INF/NaN in any case
departures.jpmml: lenient: accepts TRUE for a boolean and 1.0 for an integer (measured)
departures.basis: DataDictionary.html dataTypes are XML Schema Part 2 types; the case-insensitivity sentence of Transformations.html is about Constants (§2.6)

match.cpmml: Invalid value for field \w+: "((?!true"|false")(?i:true|false)" is not a valid boolean|[+-]?(\d+\.\d*|\.\d+|\d+(\.\d*)?[eE][+-]?\d+)" is not a valid integer|(?!-?INF"|NaN")[+-]?(?i:inf|infinity|nan)" is not a valid (double|float)|[+-]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?[dDfF]" is not a valid (double|float))

"(?!(true|false|1|0)" is not a valid boolean)(?![+-]?\d+" is not a valid integer)(?!([+-]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?|-?INF|NaN)" is not a valid (double|float))[^"]*" is not a valid (boolean|integer|double|float)

departures.cpmml: forward-referenced OutputFields and DerivedFields accepted, ordered by dependency
departures.jpmml: refuses forward OutputField references
departures.basis: leniency on invalid PMML (Q4)
departures.note: v0 generates forward DerivedField references only (ctx2), which both evaluators accept; no case is tagged output-forward-ref yet

departures.cpmml: a FieldRef to a missing predictedValue applies mapMissingTo
departures.jpmml: fails the record
departures.basis: Transformations.html FieldRef: "The optional attribute mapMissingTo may be used to map a missing result to the value specified by the attribute."

departures.cpmml: number -> boolean only for 0 and 1
departures.jpmml: measured in P0: a boolean DerivedField over integer 0/1 and over double 0.0/-0.0/1.0 gives false/true, any other value TypeCheckException -- the same rule; §8.5's 'refuses integers' does not hold for a FieldRef
departures.basis: XSD boolean lexical space {true, false, 1, 0}
departures.note: no disagreement expected from JPMML; cPMML giving true for 2, INF or NaN is B24

departures.cpmml: binary similarity measures read strings 1/0 as booleans
departures.jpmml: only true/false
departures.basis: XSD boolean lexical space
departures.note: v0 generates no clustering or KNN model

departures.cpmml: median implemented
departures.jpmml: ApplyException: Function "median" is not defined (measured, at evaluation)
departures.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html lists median among the aggregate functions

departures.cpmml: (Q1) number -> string text inside expressions is Java text, including in concat
departures.jpmml: Java text
departures.basis: concat points to XQuery fn:concat, whose casts write a whole double as 2; one text rule for the whole library is preferred (Q1)
departures.note: a departure from the spec, not from JPMML: no disagreement expected

departures.cpmml: input -0 stays -0.0
departures.jpmml: 0.0 (measured in P0: a double or float FieldRef of input -0 is 0.0)
departures.basis: XSD double has -0

departures.cpmml: ordering over a categorical or Values-less ordinal string operand evaluates with a warning
departures.jpmml: EvaluationException: Categorical value cannot be used in comparison operations (measured, for Apply and for a TreeModel SimplePredicate)
departures.basis: Q6

match.jpmml: Categorical value cannot be used in comparison operations

departures.cpmml: integer x/0 (x != 0) is invalid, not INF
departures.jpmml: invalid (N/A under asMissing)
departures.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html "If a positive number is divided by zero, INF will be returned." meets "Since INF and -INF can only be floating point numbers, they will cause floor, ceil, round, and modulo to return an invalid value."; XQuery raises err:FOAR0001 for integer division by zero
departures.note: a departure from the spec, not from JPMML: no disagreement expected; cPMML giving Infinity is B21

departures.cpmml: Discretize/MapValues without dataType take the nearest enclosing declared type
departures.jpmml: same
departures.basis: spec and XSD silent; JPMML and today's cPMML

departures.cpmml: integer-field document text with a decimal point (33.0) is a double and the field is widened to compare; a replacement or clamp bound that is not an integer widens the slot
departures.jpmml: scores
departures.basis: Functions.html implicit casts only toward less restriction (§3.4)

proposed.cpmml: an arithmetic result NaN is NaN
proposed.jpmml: EvaluationException: Function "+" returned invalid value (measured: d = NaN in +(d, INF)); the record fails
proposed.basis: Transformations.html: "All arithmetic expressions involving NaN will evaluate to NaN." Not in §8.5; proposed as D23

proposed.cpmml: a missing argument of a built-in function gives missing (then mapMissingTo/defaultValue), for every function the spec does not except
proposed.jpmml: MissingArgumentException: Function "abs" cannot accept missing value at position 0 (measured for abs, equal, threshold, floor, ceil, round, sqrt, uppercase, substring, replace, ...); + and - give missing. D3 is the case of if
proposed.basis: BuiltinFunctions.html: "Except as noted below, any missing inputs to a built-in function will result in a missing value being returned." Not in §8.5 beyond if (D3); proposed as a generalisation of D3

proposed.cpmml: an invalid value in any MiningField with invalidValueTreatment returnInvalid makes the record invalid, whether or not the model reads the field
proposed.jpmml: validates a field only when the model reads it: an invalid value in a field the expression never reads is ignored (measured)
proposed.basis: MiningSchema.html: "returnInvalid is the default and specifies that, when an invalid input is encountered, the model should return a value indicating an invalid result has been returned." Not in §8.5; proposed
proposed.note: since P2.1 (B45) both of cPMML's messages for this rule name the field ('Invalid value for field: NAME'); before, one was 'Sample: {...} didn't pass input validation', which v0 could not match
